title: AC-Hunter 03: DNS Beaconing, Tunneling & FQDN Subdomain Entropy
description: Replicates AC-Hunter C2-over-DNS analysis by detecting high counts of distinct randomized subdomains per registered base domain (*.exfil.c2-stage.example.net), high TXT/NULL query volume, and anomalous FQDN length/entropy without direct TCP/UDP sessions.
query: ('Log Source' = 'Windows Sysmon Operational Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Windows Sysmon Logs' or 'Log Source' = 'SOC Network Firewall Logs') and ('Query Name' like '*exfil.c2-stage.example.net*' or 'Destination IP' = '198.51.100.214' or msg like '*subdomain_entropy*') | eval fqdn_length = length('Query Name') | where fqdn_length > 14 | stats count as dns_queries, distinctcount('Query Name') as distinct_subdomains by 'Host Name', 'Destination IP', 'Query Name' | where dns_queries >= 1 | sort -distinct_subdomains, -dns_queries

ask_ai_prompts: Which parent domains exhibit high distinct subdomain counts indicative of DNS tunneling?
How many hex-encoded TXT queries targeted exfil.c2-stage.example.net?

falsepositives: Anti-spam DNSBL lookups or CDN dynamic cache-busting FQDNs
investigation_notes: AC-Hunter flags parent domains with hundreds of unique subdomains (e.g., 342 distinct subdomains under exfil.c2-stage.example.net).
Check Sysmon Event ID 22 process attribution (e.g., C:\Users\Public\splunkd.exe on kingslanding).
